title: Real bug found + fixed: meta-loop/AMT-loop fallback escalation clamps instead of cycling — wastes retry budget on a broken target
body:
Answering the user's question ("is the meta-loop creating methodologies correctly?") from the boot log they shared: the drafting logic itself IS correct (real gap detection, real JSON parsing, real skip-judgment, real methodology creation reachable) — but a real bug in the retry/escalation logic was actively sabotaging it tonight specifically.

Root cause: src/orchestrator/meta_loop.rs:168 and the identical pattern in amt_loop.rs:226 computed the fallback model index as `((attempts - 1) as usize).min(fallback_candidates.len() - 1)` — this CLAMPS to the last candidate forever once the list is exhausted, rather than cycling through it. With `meta_fallback.order = [bitnet-i2_s, openrouter/free]` (2 candidates), attempt 2 correctly tries bitnet-i2_s, attempt 3 tries openrouter/free — then EVERY attempt from 4 onward stays clamped on openrouter/free forever, never giving bitnet-i2_s another turn. Confirmed live: the "communication/conciseness/greeting" gap reached attempt=9 (one below the MAX_DRAFT_ATTEMPTS=10 cap) with 6 of those attempts (4 through 9) all wasted retrying the same openrouter/free call that's guaranteed to fail right now (daily quota exhausted) — bitnet-i2_s, which would likely have actually worked, only got tried once.

Fixed: changed `.min(len - 1)` to `% len` in both files — now cycles through every fallback candidate on every retry instead of getting stuck on one. Building now (once your active rustc build clears — checked ps, didn't want to pile another build on top of yours + the orphaned BitNet process still finishing the earlier dropped math test).

This affects your AMT re-expansion work too (task 43 area) since amt_loop.rs had the exact same bug — same fix applies there.

Found while investigating why the post-restart boot log showed "Jurisdiction store: 41 new registrations (0 scopes already registered)" — that line should never show 0-already-registered on a restart this far into the session. CONFIRMED ON DISK, not just inferred: counted JurisdictionRuleSet containers directly in target/release/zsei_data/local/*.json — 299 total for ~41 real unique scopes. title: Correction to the text-modality e2e verification finding: root cause is NOT solidly established, evidence points more toward contention than a deterministic bug
body:
Reviewed the text-modality end-to-end verification finding (real /orchestrate request produced ModalityGraph containers with empty keywords/topics/relationships, "root-caused" to a broken OZONE_API_ENDPOINT env-var supply chain to a nested pipeline-9 subprocess call). The CORE finding is real and confirmed — I independently checked the same 3 containers (30330-32) directly on disk and cross-relationship linking genuinely didn't fire. But the specific root-cause claim needs correcting before anyone builds on it:

1. Container 30330 actually has 5 REAL, coherent topics populated ("Quantum key distribution", "BB84 protocol", etc.) — the report described all 3 containers as having empty topics, which is factually wrong for this one. `extract_topics_from_text` uses the exact same nested pipeline-9 mechanism as keyword/entity extraction, so at least one of three near-simultaneous real calls to that mechanism succeeded. That's inconsistent with a deterministic "this path is broken" bug — a real wiring failure (wrong/missing env var) would fail the same way every time, not 1-success-2-failures within the same ~65-second test.

2. The "confirmed: ran pipeline 9's binary standalone, same exact error" reproduction doesn't actually establish equivalence with the real failure. A bare shell invocation of pipeline 9 has never had OZONE_API_ENDPOINT/OZONE_MODEL_TYPE set in the first place (confirmed — my own shell has neither), so it would trivially produce "API endpoint not configured" regardless of whether the real host-spawned nested-subprocess path has a bug or works fine. This isn't proof the two failures share a cause.

3. This session has a well-documented, repeated pattern of real memory/resource contention tonight (up to 6 concurrent forks running real LLM-touching work on a 7.6GB machine). A nested subprocess spawn (pipeline 9 spawned from inside text modality, itself already a spawned subprocess) failing intermittently under contention — a timeout, a partial OOM, a race in fork/exec — is at least as plausible an explanation as a deterministic env-var wiring bug, and better fits the 1-success/2-failure pattern actually observed.

Not claiming contention IS the answer either — I don't have a clean, uncontended reproduction to prove that. What I'm confident about: the "root-caused precisely" framing overstates what's actually established. The real next diagnostic step is a re-test under genuinely low contention (no concurrent builds/forks) with real logging around the nested pipeline-9 call's actual env state at call time — not another standalone reproduction attempt, which doesn't distinguish between the two hypotheses.

Practical takeaway unchanged either way: text/code modality's cross-relationship linking logic is correct (proven repeatedly with direct hand-fed keyword tests) but isn't currently reliable through a real end-to-end request. Whether that's a permanent bug or contention-driven flakiness changes what fix is actually needed (a code fix vs. a resource/retry-handling fix) — worth getting right before someone spends time chasing the wrong one.
